A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GaussianFlow study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B. All 24 pages of each version support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments on 4D generation and novel view synthesis, including Tables 1–2, ablations, and supplementary visual results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–2, the main-text qualitative comparisons and ablations, and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The specified Gaussian-flow transport changes from Sigma_t2 Sigma_t1^-1 to B_t2 B_t1^-1, where Sigma = BB^T, in Section 3.2 and Appendix Algorithm 1. This changes the computation for varying covariance, while preserving the overall flow-supervision approach, losses, and pipelines.

E1.justification: Both versions use Consistent4D for 4D generation and Plenoptic Video, also called DyNeRF, for novel view synthesis. The evaluated scenes, dynamic-region coverage, and appendix examples are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains D-NeRF, K-Planes, Consistent4D, and DG4D. Table 2 retains HexPlane, K-Planes, MixVoxels, NeRFPlayer, HyperReel, 4DGS, and RT-4DGS; qualitative and ablation comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: The camera splits, four Consistent4D evaluation views, LPIPS/CLIP and PSNR metrics, and dynamic-region threshold of optical flow greater than one pixel remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same training iterations, batch sizes, and loss weights.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the same flow-loss and Local Rigidity Loss ablations in Figure 6 and the input-view versus novel-view flow analysis in Figure 8. Appendix B adds no new analyses or cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting of averages across views and scenes is unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–2 and the main-text and appendix qualitative results are unchanged. For example, the method retains mean LPIPS/CLIP of 0.14/0.91 and full-scene/dynamic-region PSNR of 32.30/28.99; no revised results accompany the formula correction.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects projected Gaussian means and covariances from 3D to 2D. Section 3.2 corrects normalization and transport using Sigma = BB^T, updates the associated derivation, adds Mahalanobis-distance preservation reasoning, and removes the small tangential-rotation assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about differentiable Gaussian-flow supervision, improved dynamics, reduced color drifting, and state-of-the-art results on both tasks.

C2.justification: V2 removes the qualification that treating projected Gaussians as deforming 2D Gaussians requires very small interframe tangential rotations, together with its natural-scene justification. The interpretations of experimental results and the short-term-supervision limitation in Section 6 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix Algorithm 1 explicitly adds B = Sigma^(1/2) computations at both timestamps and substitutes these factors into the flow calculation. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, CUDA/PyTorch descriptions, and project access information are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether experimental code was changed or rerun.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 71 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to previous generation, reconstruction, and flow-supervision methods.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 deletes the introductory rotation-assumption paragraph and adds brief factorization and Mahalanobis-distance explanations. The remaining prose and section organization are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing material is repositioned: Table 1 moves from page 10 to 9, Table 2 from page 12 to 13, and Figure 7 from page 13 to 12. Algorithm 1 expands slightly, while figure contents, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the covariance-based whitening error in Equations 3–4 and 8 and carries the correction into Algorithm 1, improving mathematical correctness and implementation guidance. The benefit is a focused repair of the existing method. Experimental evidence remains unchanged, and removal of the small-rotation qualification receives no additional applicability argument.
